question_or_proposition: Under the FLOATING SOLIDS OR VISIBLE FOAM provision, does the clause 'that would cause the formation of a visible sheen or visible deposits on the bottom or shoreline, or would damage or impair the normal growth, function or reproduction of human, animal, plant or aquatic life' specify the conditions that must be met for a discharge of oils, scum, grease, or other floating materials to violate the prohibition (permitting discharge that does not produce those effects), or does the provision prohibit any discharge of those materials irrespective of whether such effects occur?
required_context: FLOATING SOLIDS OR VISIBLE FOAM section heading and discharge prohibition text (Page 5, Part I)
Absence of explicit monitoring frequency or sample-type table within this section, contrasted with adjacent sections that specify monitoring schedules
source_locator: gcc/final_permit.pdf Page: 5, Section: part_i, FLOATING SOLIDS OR VISIBLE FOAM
notes: Resolution of the causation clause determines what evidence is needed to establish compliance or violation for a narrative/visual standard without numeric limits, which in turn affects whether applicable monitoring obligations can be identified and how missing or non-numeric evidence should be classified.
